- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect bearish sentiment’s fading or reversal.
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+), producing exaggerated highs in next period; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.3), model fails to adjust quickly; delay or reduce forecast increase until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often continues downward; if sentiment is neutral, add slight upward bias to avoid prolonged bearish drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (especially after 20–25 days); add 2–5% buffer to forecast from day 20 onward if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over 5+ days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for potential rebound or policy-driven lift.
